thesis: 시장 유동성과 신용 스프레드는 아직 스트레스 국면이 아니지만, Fed의 9월 재인상과 중동 전쟁에 따른 에너지·해상운송 충격이 동시에 존재한다. 글로벌 무역 분절도 높다. NU의 펀더멘털 점수는 변경하지 않되 신규 매수 pacing은 0.5배로 제한한다. 현재 확인된 충격 중 Brazil/Mexico/Colombia에 대한 영구 시장접근 상실이나 제재는 없다.

evidence.claim: Fed raised the federal-funds target by 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% on 2026-09-16.
Chicago Fed NFCI was -0.560 for the week ending 2026-09-11, indicating financial conditions looser than historical average despite the policy hike.
U.S. aggregate high-yield OAS was 2.68% on Sep. 18 and BB OAS 1.55%, while CCC-and-lower spreads remained above 10.7%, showing ample broad liquidity but weak-tier bifurcation.
VIX spot was 14.87 on Sep. 21, inconsistent with a broad market liquidity crisis.
Hormuz and Red Sea shipping remained heavily disrupted by the U.S.-Iran conflict and Houthi advances, with sharply reduced vessel traffic and costly alternative oil-routing arrangements.
Brazil-U.S. tariff talks, the USMCA review and broader WTO fragmentation remain active; these raise global policy uncertainty but do not establish permanent NU-specific market-access loss.

counterevidence: NFCI and VIX indicate financial markets remain loose rather than systemically stressed.
Broad high-yield and BB spreads are tight, so external credit availability is still strong.
NU is predominantly a domestic financial-services platform in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia and has little direct exposure to Middle East shipping routes.
Brazil and Mexico tariff disputes remain under negotiation rather than constituting a permanent loss of market access.
unknowns: Duration and inflation pass-through of the current Middle East energy shock.
Whether the September Fed hike develops into a sustained tightening cycle.
How USMCA and Brazil-U.S. tariff negotiations resolve after the cutoff.
Second-order FX and funding effects on Latin American banks if oil and U.S. rates stay elevated.
falsifiers: A durable Middle East ceasefire and normalized Hormuz/Red Sea traffic would justify lifting geopolitical pacing.
Fed returns to a neutral/easing path while broad credit remains open, supporting a higher financial-conditions multiplier.
A Brazil/Mexico-specific sanction, nationalization or durable market-access loss would require fundamental reanalysis rather than pacing only.

key_kpis.name: Fed target / global real rates
key_kpis.threshold: sustained further hikes keep pacing constrained

key_kpis.name: HY OAS / NFCI
key_kpis.threshold: HY OAS >4% or NFCI >0 signals material credit tightening

key_kpis.name: Hormuz/Red Sea traffic
key_kpis.threshold: persistent disruption keeps geopolitical multiplier at 0.5

next_checks: Next FOMC decision and inflation path.

financial_conditions.summary: Global market pricing remains relatively loose, but the U.S. policy impulse turned tighter. The Fed raised the funds target to 3.75%-4.00% on Sep. 16 while the Chicago Fed NFCI remained materially below zero and VIX closed at 14.87 on Sep. 21. Treat as moderate tightening risk rather than broad financial stress.

credit_liquidity.summary: Broad U.S. credit liquidity is still open: aggregate high-yield OAS was 2.68% on Sep. 18 and BB OAS 1.55%. Lower-quality credit is more fragile, with CCC-and-lower spreads above 10.7%. This is not a funding freeze, but risk premia offer limited cushion outside the weakest tier.

geopolitical_events.summary: The active U.S.-Iran conflict and Houthi advances create high military, energy and maritime-shipping risk around Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. These are global pacing risks; no permanent NU-specific market-access event is identified.

structural_trade.summary: Trade fragmentation remains high. Brazil-U.S. tariff negotiations and the USMCA review are active, while U.S.-China technology restrictions and Russia/Iran sanctions remain structural global frictions. No durable NU-specific market-access loss is established.
